item.title: Tui Nayau reminds youths that Fiji’s future is in their hands
item.description: The Tui Nayau, Ratu Tevita Lutunauga Kapaiwai Uluilakeba Mara is urging young Fijians to value education, learn their languages, understand their cultural roots and develop skills that will help shape the country’s future. In his Fiji Day message from Lakeba, Ratu Tevita says independence is not something to be taken for granted, but a responsibility every generation must uphold.
item.content:encoded:
The Tui Nayau, Ratu Tevita Lutunauga Kapaiwai Uluilakeba Mara is urging young Fijians to value education, learn their languages, understand their cultural roots and develop skills that will help shape the country’s future.

In his Fiji Day message from Lakeba, Ratu Tevita says independence is not something to be taken for granted, but a responsibility every generation must uphold.

He says young people have an important role in protecting Fiji’s future through honest work, service to their families and communities, and the courage to reject things that threatened their lives and homes.

As Fiji marks 56 years of independence, the Gone Turaga Bale na Tui Nayau, Sau ni Vanua ko Lau and Tui Lau says the anniversary is an opportunity for Fijians to renew their commitment to national unity, peace and cooperation.

He says Fiji’s independence was achieved through dialogue, patience and goodwill, with leaders from different communities choosing a shared future.

Ratu Tevita also paid tribute to the chiefs, elected leaders, faith leaders and ordinary Fijians who contributed to the country’s independence, including the late Tui Nayau and Fiji’s first Prime Minister, Ratu Sir Kamisese Mara.

He says their contributions laid the foundation for the nation, but the responsibility of building Fiji had been passed on to the present generation.

Speaking on behalf of the Vanua of Lau, Ratu Tevita highlighted the importance of protecting Fiji’s marine resources, traditions and cultural heritage for future generations.

He says traditional leadership was rooted in service and that Fiji’s diversity of faiths, cultures and languages are one of its greatest strengths.

Ratu Tevita is also calling on Fijians to practise peace, mutual respect and cooperation in their homes, villages, workplaces and places of worship.

He extendes his Fiji Day greetings to Fijians living abroad, acknowledging their contributions and reminding them that they remained part of the nation wherever they lived.

item.title: From CWM Hospital to Australia, Vedika Roy continues her nursing journey
item.description: The nursing experience and values gained in Fiji have provided a strong foundation for Fiji-trained nurse Vedika Roy as she continues working towards becoming a registered nurse in Australia. Roy says although moving to a new country and adjusting to a different healthcare system brought moments of doubt, she reminded herself that she was not starting from zero.
item.content:encoded:
The nursing experience and values gained in Fiji have provided a strong foundation for Fiji-trained nurse Vedika Roy as she continues working towards becoming a registered nurse in Australia.

Roy says although moving to a new country and adjusting to a different healthcare system brought moments of doubt, she reminded herself that she was not starting from zero.

She says she carried with her the knowledge, experience and values gained through years of studying and working as a nurse in Fiji.

Roy began her nursing journey at the Fiji School of Nursing under Fiji National University in 2013 and graduated in 2016.

After completing a one-year internship at CWM Hospital, she pursued paediatric nursing and later worked in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.

She says caring for newborn babies and supporting their families was one of the most meaningful parts of her nursing career in Fiji, teaching her compassion, patience and resilience.

Roy later moved to Australia for personal and professional reasons, where she had to adjust to a different healthcare system and approach to nursing practice.

She says there were challenging moments when she questioned herself, but she remained determined and continued working towards her goals, one step at a time.

After moving to Australia, Roy completed an Advanced Diploma in Leadership and Management in Nursing before pursuing a Master of Nursing at the Institute of Health and Management.

She says her studies have helped strengthen her confidence and understanding of nursing practice in Australia, while also developing her interest in nursing research and evidence-based practice.

Roy says the experience and values she gained while working in Fiji continue to guide her as she works towards becoming a registered nurse in Australia .

She says moving overseas was not the end of her nursing journey, but the beginning of a new chapter built on the foundation of her training and experience in Fiji.

Roy is encouraging other internationally qualified nurses and nursing students to believe in themselves, take one step at a time and avoid comparing their journeys with those of others.
